reference: Steady multizone air-flow network with the square-root opening law, the stack pressure term and the zone mass balance, re-implemented from ASHRAE Fundamentals ch. 16 / CIBSE Guide A and solved with scipy.optimize.root (Powell hybrid) followed by a Newton polish; the series cascade is compared against a closed form that uses no solver at all.
reference_citations: ASHRAE Handbook - Fundamentals (2021), chapter 16 "Ventilation and Infiltration": orifice flow Q = Cd A sqrt(2 dp / rho) and the thermal (stack) pressure dp = g h (rho_o - rho_i).
CIBSE Guide A, "Environmental design", appendix 4A: flow through purpose-provided openings and discharge coefficients for doors, grilles and gaps.

G.N. Walton, "AIRNET - a computer program for building airflow network modeling", NISTIR 89-4072, National Institute of Standards and Technology, 1989: the node mass balance of a multizone network and its Newton solution.
tolerance: The network is a closed-form algebraic system, so the reference is exact: scipy.optimize.root followed by a Newton polish leaves a node residual below 1e-14 m3/s, and the three series-cascade cases are compared against a hand-derived closed form that uses no solver at all. The tool stops its own damped Newton at a node residual of 1e-10 m3/s (3.6e-7 m3/h), so pressures are graded at 1e-8 relative or 1e-7 Pa absolute, flows at 1e-8 relative or 1e-6 m3/h absolute, whichever is looser - both far above the solver stopping criterion and far below anything the interface prints. The bookkeeping identities (every zone balance closing on the reported flows, supply minus extract equalling the net envelope flow, velocity equalling flow over effective area, independence from the order of the blocks) are exact arithmetic and are held to 1e-9 relative.
not_benchmarked: The 0.04 Pa regularisation of the square-root law is a declared modelling choice; the reference reproduces it and the harness records how many connections sit inside that window per case, but the size of the error it introduces against the unregularised law is not graded.
Discharge coefficients, closed-door gap areas and the default coefficient library are assumptions with their own provenance badges in the interface; they are inputs here, not graded quantities.

The heat, moisture and contaminant transport (the linear well-mixed system over the solved flows) and the capture-velocity relation are outside this benchmark, which covers the pressure and flow network only.
Wind pressure, fan curves, duct networks and every transient are outside the model.
The page shows its own built-in checks. Those re-run the same solver and are a self-check of consistency, not validation; nothing in this artifact relies on them.
run_notes: Each network is loaded through the tool's own permalink codec and read back from Diagram.record.build().
Cross-check: on the three series cascades the reference's network solver and the hand-derived closed form agree to better than 1e-10 relative, and the tool matches both.
crosscheck: closed-form series cascade vs. the scipy network solve: < 1e-10 relative on every room pressure and every connection flow.

cases.note: The rooms carry a cleanliness rank. In the shipped building the cascade must fall monotonically from rank 1 to rank 4, the cleanest room must sit above ambient and the dirtiest below it, and the sign convention must hold: a room in over-pressure loses air through its envelope leakage, a room in under-pressure gains it.

A single room fed by an imposed 3600 m3/h through a 0.10 m2 leak must settle at +rho/2*(Q/(Cd*A))^2 with air leaving through the leak; the same room on an imposed extract must settle at the mirror-image negative pressure with air entering. At building level, supply above extract must push air out through the envelope and extract above supply must pull it in.
a sealed room with an imposed supply and no way out: there is no steady state, and the pressure the model would need is unbounded
